title: Keep a performance checklist
summary: A useful performance budget sets limits that matter for the page.
introduction: A useful performance budget sets limits that matter for the page. Your task: Choose one size or timing to track for your project.
learningObjectives: Choose one size or timing to track for your project.
Explain the example for keep a performance checklist

blocks.text: A useful performance budget sets limits that matter for the page. Recheck after changes so a fast page does not slowly become heavy.

Use a local test page and browser developer tools. Code samples show a page choice or a measurement. Compare before and after under the same conditions; exact timings depend on the device and network.

blocks.code:
List important pages and tasks.
Track total transferred image and script sizes.
Check a slower device and network.
Review LCP, INP and CLS evidence.
Keep accessibility and readable content in every check.
Repeat after large new features.
blocks.title: Keep a performance checklist

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: Transfer size measures what must be downloaded; it is not the same as how quickly the page responds.
Repeating the same important tasks catches regressions after a new feature is added.

blocks.text: The project gets a repeatable check, not a one-time speed score.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not remove useful labels, error messages or accessible controls to make a benchmark smaller.
